name: Ceasefire Dilation

detectability.signature: Subtle chronometric distortion field detectable only by high-precision tachyon clocks

proximity: Ship chronometers begin to drift, losing approximately 0.3 seconds per hour relative to galactic standard
Crew members feel a subjective sense of calm and decreased urgency
Reaction times slow measurably without the affected individual's awareness
contact: Time passes at roughly 60% of normal rate within the dilation field
External communications become asynchronous, with noticeable delay distortion
Metabolic processes slow proportionally, effectively extending biological lifespan while inside
prolonged_exposure: Cumulative temporal debt accumulates—weeks inside may correspond to months outside
Re-entry to normal spacetime causes severe disorientation and temporal vertigo lasting days
Long-term residents develop a persistent subjective sense that normal time moves 'too fast'

age: Estimated 2.1 billion years, likely a relic of early stellar formation in this region
phenomena: Projectiles fired into the field visibly decelerate, hanging in space like frozen rain
Light entering the boundary undergoes a slight redshift, giving the interior a warm amber tint
Biological organisms within the field age more slowly, with measurable telomere preservation
Sound-carrying media within the field produce noticeably lower-pitched tones
hazards: Temporal debt makes the field dangerous for anyone on a time-sensitive mission or schedule
The field's invisibility means ships can enter it unknowingly if sensors are poorly calibrated
opportunities: Medical facilities use the field's edge for slowing the progression of terminal illnesses
The field provides a natural sanctuary where pursuing fleets cannot maintain tactical coordination
Long-duration experiments benefit from the extended subjective time available to researchers inside
known_incidents: During the Kethani Border War, the retreating 3rd Flotilla entered the Ceasefire Dilation to buy time for reinforcements; their pursuers, unwilling to accept the temporal cost, broke off the engagement—the first recorded use of the anomaly as a tactical refuge
description: The Ceasefire Dilation is a vast elliptical region of slowed time, spanning approximately 31,000 kilometers along its major axis. It is entirely invisible to the naked eye, detectable only through precision chronometric instruments that register the temporal gradient at its boundary. Objects and beings within the field experience time at roughly 60% of the normal rate, a gentle but cumulative effect that has profound implications for anyone who lingers.

The field's most notable property is its effect on conflict. Weapons fire decelerates visibly upon crossing the boundary, tactical communications fall out of sync, and coordinated fleet maneuvers become impossible. These properties have made the Ceasefire Dilation a de facto sanctuary—a place where the physics of war simply stop working efficiently. The name was coined after a famous incident in which a retreating fleet used the field to halt a pursuit without firing a shot.

The anomaly is natural in origin, estimated to be over two billion years old, likely a fossil of some gravitational or temporal process during the region's stellar formation epoch. It predates all known spacefaring civilizations by an enormous margin. There is no evidence of artificial construction or modification, though some fringe theorists argue that any natural process producing such a clean, stable temporal field is itself suspect.

Today the Ceasefire Dilation is used primarily as a medical facility zone and a site for long-duration scientific research. A ring of stations orbits just outside the boundary, housing patients whose terminal conditions are slowed by periodic immersion in the field. Diplomatic tradition holds that hostilities are suspended within the dilation, a custom that has been honored more often than not. The anomaly serves as a quiet reminder that some problems can only be solved by slowing down.
